exams.name: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya Selection Test (JNVST) – Class VI
exams.summary: A single, free, district-specific selection test for admission to Class VI in a JNV. JNVs are free co-educational residential schools for Classes VI–XII; education, board and lodging, uniform and textbooks are free.

content.forSchools: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas — 665 functional residential schools; Delhi has JNVs at Mungeshpur and Jaffarpur Kalan
eligibility: Bona fide resident of the district where admission is sought, studying in Class V in 2026-27 in a Government, Government-aided or recognised school (or NIOS “B” certificate).
Born between 01.05.2015 and 31.07.2017 (both dates inclusive).
Must have studied Classes III, IV and V for full academic sessions; candidates who skipped a class or already passed Class V are not eligible.
A candidate can appear only once — repeaters are disqualified.
Rural-quota candidates must have studied Classes III–V in rural-area schools.

pattern.title: Single paper — 80 objective questions, 100 marks, 2 hours
notes: 1.25 marks per correct answer; no negative marking.
Minimum qualifying marks: 14 in Mental Ability & EVS, 7 in Arithmetic, 7 in Language.
OMR sheet, blue/black ball-point pen only; 40 extra minutes for Divyang candidates.
Delhi candidates can take the test in English or Hindi; the medium cannot be changed later.

topics: Pattern completion (incl. alphabet and number patterns)
The natural world, our surroundings, basic science and social-science awareness
Number system, place value, ascending/descending order
Measurement of length, mass, capacity, time, money; unit conversion
Types of angles, directions and mapping
Data handling: bar diagrams, tables, pictographs
Four passages, five questions each — reading comprehension

selection: Merit in the selection test, district-wise. At least 75% of seats for rural candidates; the rest are open.
At least one-third of seats for girls; SC/ST as per district population (minimum 15% SC and 7.5% ST); 27% OBC (Central list); Divyang reservation as per GOI norms.
Ties broken by Mental Ability & EVS marks, then Arithmetic, then category and age rules in the prospectus.
Provisional selection is confirmed only after document verification at the JNV.
content.fee: Application is free. In JNVs, Classes VI–VIII are free; a Vidyalaya Vikas Nidhi of ₹600/month is collected in Classes IX–XII (SC/ST, Divyang, girls and BPL students are exempt).

preparation.step: Read the prospectus and check eligibility first
preparation.detail: Confirm the date-of-birth window, district of residence, and whether the Class III–V schools count as rural or urban — this decides your quota.

preparation.step: Learn the five Mental Ability question types
preparation.detail: Practise pattern completion, figure series, geometric completion, mirror/water images and embedded figures daily; these are non-verbal and improve fast with practice.

preparation.step: Cover the 12 Arithmetic topics
preparation.detail: Use the Class 3–5 maths textbook; focus on fractions, measurement and units, area/perimeter and reading bar graphs and pictographs.

preparation.step: Build reading comprehension
preparation.detail: Read one short passage a day in the exam medium and answer questions on it — the Language test is four passages with five questions each.

preparation.step: Revise EVS from the Class 3–5 books
preparation.detail: Plants, animals, water, transport, maps, our country — EVS now carries 25 marks.

preparation.step: Solve the official 2026 paper and the prospectus samples under time
preparation.detail: Keep to 60/30/30 minutes per section and practise OMR marking with a ball-point pen.

preparation.step: Secure the qualifying marks in every section
preparation.detail: You must reach 14, 7 and 7 marks in the three sections — do not leave a section weak.

faq.question: Is there an application fee for JNVST?
faq.answer: No. The prospectus states that registration for the selection test is free.

faq.question: Can a child appear in JNVST more than once?
faq.answer: No. A candidate can appear only once; repeaters are disqualified.

faq.question: Which district should we apply in?
faq.answer: The district where the child is a bona fide resident and studying in Class V, as defined in the prospectus.

content.languages: English, Hindi and regional languages as listed in the prospectus
examDay: The selection test runs from 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.; Divyang candidates get 40 minutes extra.
Mark answers on the OMR sheet with a blue or black ball-point pen only.

dates.note: The prospectus says the result is expected by the end of March 2027.

exams.name: Navodaya Vidyalaya Lateral Entry Selection Test – Class IX
exams.summary: A district-wise test for admission to Class IX in a Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, only against seats likely to be vacant in 2027-28. JNVs are free co-educational residential schools affiliated to CBSE.

content.forSchools: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas — 665 functional residential schools in 27 states and 8 UTs (not Tamil Nadu); only vacant Class IX seats
eligibility: Bona fide resident of the district where admission is sought, and studying Class VIII in 2026-27 in a Government or Government-recognised school of that same district.
Born between 01.05.2012 and 31.07.2014 (both dates inclusive) — for all categories, including SC/ST/OBC/Divyang.
Indian nationals studying Class VIII in India only.
Not eligible: students who passed Class VIII in an earlier session, or who already appeared in the lateral entry test in the previous session.
Rural quota: the Class VIII school must be in a rural area; a single day of Class VIII in an urban school makes the candidate urban.

pattern.title: One paper — 100 objective questions, 100 marks, 2½ hours (Class VIII level)
notes: OMR answer sheet, blue/black ball-point pen; one mark per correct answer and no negative marking.
Minimum qualifying marks (as per NVS criteria) are needed in all four subjects.
Merit is on Mathematics + Science + the better of the two languages.
Medium: English or Hindi, chosen in the form and not changed later. Divyang candidates get 50 minutes extra.

topics: Squares and square roots; cubes and cube roots
Comparing quantities: percentage, profit and loss, discount, simple and compound interest
Mensuration: area of plane figures; surface area and volume of cube, cuboid and cylinder
Data handling: bar graph, pie chart, probability
Class VIII Hindi grammar and an unseen passage, as listed in the prospectus

selection: Seats are only those likely to be vacant in the JNV concerned in 2027-28; vacancies may change, and provisional selection gives no right to admission.
Vacant SC/ST/OBC/Divyang seats go to candidates of those categories; OBC as per the central list.
Ties: girls first, then higher marks in two subjects out of 30, then higher total out of 100, then the younger candidate.
Admission needs passing Class VIII in 2026-27 and verification of residence, age, school, category and rural/urban status.
No re-evaluation or re-totalling; marks are not communicated.
content.fee: No application fee: the prospectus says registration on the NVS portal and the JNV help desks are free of cost. Education, board and lodging, uniform and textbooks are free in JNVs. A Vidyalaya Vikas Nidhi of ₹600 a month is collected in Classes IX–XII; SC/ST, Divyang and girl students and BPL families are exempt. Wards of government employees (other than exempted categories) pay ₹1,500 a month or the Children Education Allowance received, whichever is less, but not less than ₹600.

preparation.step: Check the district rule first
preparation.detail: Residence and the Class VIII school must both be in the district of the JNV you apply to.

preparation.step: Give Mathematics and Science most of your time
preparation.detail: They carry 70 of 100 marks and always count towards merit.

preparation.step: Do not neglect either language
preparation.detail: You need qualifying marks in English and Hindi, and the better one counts towards merit.

preparation.step: Work through the Class VIII NCERT chapters listed
preparation.detail: The syllabus follows the Class VIII Science and Mathematics books chapter by chapter.

preparation.step: Practise the official previous paper on an OMR sheet
preparation.detail: Time yourself to 2½ hours; there is no negative marking, so answer every question.

documents: Birth certificate issued by the competent Government authority
Residence certificate of the parent for the district of the JNV (same district as the Class VIII school)
Rural-area certificate for the Class VIII school (rural quota)
Aadhaar card of the candidate
Divyang certificate, if applicable
OBC certificate (central list), if applicable
For registration: photograph and signatures of the candidate and a parent (JPG, 10–100 KB)

faq.question: Can a child who missed JNVST in Class V apply now?
faq.answer: Yes, if studying Class VIII in 2026-27 in a recognised school of the JNV's district and born between 01.05.2012 and 31.07.2014 — but only vacant seats are filled.

faq.question: Is there an application fee?
faq.answer: No. Registration on the NVS portal is free, and every JNV has a free help desk.

faq.question: How many seats are there?
faq.answer: Only seats likely to be vacant; the prospectus attaches a tentative vacancy list and says vacancies may change.

papers.title: Class IX lateral entry question booklet
papers.note: Published on the NVS Class IX application portal

content.papersNote: NVS publishes one previous question booklet on the application portal. We did not find official answer keys, so none are listed.
applicationSteps: Apply online only, on the NVS application portal linked from navodaya.gov.in. Registration is free and can be done from a desktop, laptop, mobile or tablet.
Keep ready: photograph, the parent's signature and the candidate's signature (JPG, 10–100 KB each), Aadhaar number, APAAR ID/PEN, Class VIII school details and address.
Every JNV has a free help desk that uploads applications — take the candidate, the photograph and both signatures.
What you enter is treated as final. A correction window for selected fields opens for two days after the last date; no changes are allowed after that.
examDay: Download the admit card free from the application portal (NVS plans to release it about a month before the test).
Mark answers on the OMR sheet with a blue or black ball-point pen only — pencils are not allowed, and striking, erasing or correction fluid make an answer invalid.
The test runs for 2½ hours without a break; Divyang candidates get 50 minutes extra.
The medium chosen in the form (English or Hindi) cannot be changed.

dates.label: Last date to register online (free)
dates.note: Some news reports mention later extensions in October 2026; we could not find an NVS extension notice to check. Applications are closed in either case.

dates.label: Selection test (2½ hours, at the district JNV or allotted centre)

exams.name: Navodaya Vidyalaya Lateral Entry Selection Test – Class XI
exams.summary: A test for admission to Class XI (Science, Commerce or Humanities) in a Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya, against seats likely to be vacant in 2027-28 after JNV students move up. District merit first, then a state merit list.

content.forSchools: Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas — free CBSE residential schools; only vacant Class XI seats in the streams each JNV offers
content.entryClassText: Class XI (session 2027-28), Science / Commerce / Humanities, against vacant seats
eligibility: Born between 01.06.2010 and 31.07.2012 (both dates inclusive) — for all categories.

Studying Class X in 2026-27 (April–March or January–December session) in a Government or Government-recognised school of the district where the JNV is located; students who passed Class X earlier are not eligible.
Indian nationals studying Class X in India only.
Candidates from one state are not eligible for admission in another state.

pattern.title: One paper — 100 objective questions, 100 marks, 2½ hours (11:00 a.m. – 1:30 p.m.)
notes: Bilingual (English and Hindi) question paper; OMR answer sheet.
Divyang candidates get 50 minutes extra.

topics: Reading: discursive and case-based unseen passages (10)
Grammar: tenses, modals, subject–verb concord, reported speech, determiners, spelling, syntax (10)
Polynomials; pair of linear equations; quadratic equations; arithmetic progressions
Geometry and the rest of the Class X syllabus, as listed in the prospectus
Class X level, as listed in Annexure-I of the prospectus

selection: Only seats likely to be vacant after JNV Class X students are admitted to Class XI, subject to accommodation.
District merit list first (residence and Class X study in that district), then a state-level merit list for remaining vacancies in the state.
Apply for up to two streams; options are considered in the order Science, Commerce, Humanities.
Rural/Girl/SC/ST/OBC/Divyang vacancies go to those categories; provisional selection gives no right to admission until documents are verified.
Result likely by May/June 2027 on the application portal; no re-evaluation, and marks are not communicated.
content.fee: No application fee: registration on the NVS portal is free of cost. Education, board and lodging, uniform and textbooks are free in JNVs. A Vidyalaya Vikas Nidhi of ₹600 a month is collected in Classes IX–XII; SC/ST, Divyang and girl students and BPL families are exempt. Wards of government employees (other than exempted categories) pay ₹1,500 a month or the Children Education Allowance received, whichever is less, but not less than ₹600.

preparation.step: Decide your streams before you register
preparation.detail: You can opt for at most two, and options are considered Science first, then Commerce, then Humanities.

preparation.step: Balance all five sections
preparation.detail: Each carries 20 marks; Mental Ability rewards daily practice with figure and coding questions.

preparation.step: Revise the Class X NCERT books
preparation.detail: Mathematics, Science and Social Science questions follow the Class X syllabus listed in the prospectus.

preparation.step: Keep Class X on track
preparation.detail: Admission also needs passing Class X in 2026-27 and the documents listed below.

documents: Birth certificate issued by the competent Government authority
Class X pass certificate
Residence certificate for the district (for district-merit selection)
Rural-area certificate for the Class X school (rural quota)
Aadhaar card of the candidate
Divyang certificate, if applicable
OBC certificate (central list), if applicable

faq.question: Can a student from another state get a seat?
faq.answer: No. The prospectus says candidates from one state are not eligible for admission in another state.

faq.question: Which streams can I choose?
faq.answer: Science, Commerce and Humanities, as offered by the JNV — up to two, considered in that order.

content.papersNote: We did not find an officially published previous Class XI paper or answer key on the NVS portal, so none are listed.
applicationSteps: Apply online only, free of cost, on the NVS application portal linked from navodaya.gov.in.
Choose at most two streams; options are considered in the order Science, Commerce, Humanities.
Every JNV has a free help desk that uploads applications.
Fill in details with care — they are taken as final. A correction window for selected fields opens briefly after the last date; no corrections are entertained after it.
examDay: Download the admit card from the NVS application portal and bring a valid ID issued by a Government authority; the photo on the admit card is matched at the centre.
Sit the test only at the centre shown on the admit card — requests to change centre are not accepted.
The test runs from 11:00 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. with a bilingual (English and Hindi) paper and an OMR answer sheet; Divyang candidates get 50 minutes extra.
Use a blue or black ball-point pen on the OMR sheet; pencils are not allowed.

dates.label: Last date to register online (free)
dates.note: Some news reports mention later extensions in October 2026; we could not find an NVS extension notice to check. Applications are closed in either case.

dates.label: Result on the application portal
dates.note: The prospectus says the result is likely by May/June 2027.

exams.name: All India Sainik Schools Entrance Examination (AISSEE) – Class VI & IX
exams.conductingAuthority: National Testing Agency (NTA) for the Sainik Schools Society (Ministry of Defence)
exams.summary: A national pen-and-paper (OMR) multiple-choice exam. Admission is by e-counselling on the school-wise, gender-wise, category-wise (home state / outside state) merit list, medical fitness and document verification.

content.forSchools: 33 Sainik Schools and approved New Sainik Schools — English-medium CBSE residential schools that prepare cadets for NDA and other officer academies
eligibility: Class IX (2026-27 cycle): 13–15 years as on 31.03.2026 — born 01.04.2011 to 31.03.2013, and passed Class VIII.
Girls are eligible to apply (for approved New Sainik Schools, check the school’s own admission policy).
Home State vs Outside State is decided by the candidate’s domicile and the location of the Sainik School chosen.
Check the current year’s bulletin: age windows move forward by one year each cycle.

pattern.title: Class VI — 125 questions, 300 marks, 150 minutes
notes: Mathematics: 3 marks per question; other sections 2 marks each.
Available in English, Hindi and 11 regional languages (bilingual booklet).

pattern.title: Class IX — 150 questions, 400 marks, 180 minutes
notes: Mathematics: 4 marks per question; other sections 2 marks each.
Medium: English only.

topics: Natural numbers, LCM & HCF, unitary method, fractions, ratio & proportion
Profit & loss, simplification, average, percentage, simple interest
Area & perimeter, lines & angles, complementary/supplementary angles, types of angles, circle
Conversion of units, Roman numerals, volume of cube & cuboid, prime & composite numbers
Plane figures, decimals, speed & time, operations on numbers, temperature, arranging fractions
Comprehension passage, vocabulary, synonyms/antonyms, idioms & phrases
Parts of speech: nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, articles, interjections
Tenses, types of sentences, question tags, sentence formation and word order
Spelling, confusing words, gender, number, singular/plural, collective nouns, rhyming words
National symbols; India at a glance; art & culture; awards; personalities (current)
Indian defence system; sports; national & international organisations
Solar system & earth; mountains; water cycle; energy; climate & natural calamities
Water in daily life; digestion & food preservation; farming; tribal communities & forests
Scientific devices; water pollution & microbial diseases; humans, plants and animals

selection: Qualifying standard in the bulletin: at least 25% marks in each subject and 40% in aggregate (see the bulletin for category-specific rules).
School-wise, gender-wise and category-wise (Home State / Outside State) merit lists, followed by e-counselling.
Medical fitness and original-document verification at the allotted school.
Approved New Sainik Schools fill at least 40% of seats from AISSEE merit (Category A).
content.fee: AISSEE-2026 application fee: ₹850 (General / Defence / OBC-NCL), ₹700 (SC/ST). School fees differ by Sainik School — see each school’s fee structure.

preparation.step: Download the current NTA bulletin
preparation.detail: Note the age window, your home state, and the Sainik Schools you can choose; the merit list is school-wise.

preparation.step: Give Mathematics the most time
preparation.detail: For Class VI it is 150 of 300 marks; for Class IX, 200 of 400. Work through every topic in the syllabus list with timed practice.

preparation.step: Practise Intelligence daily
preparation.detail: Analogies, series, classification and coding questions improve quickly with 20–25 questions a day.

preparation.step: Strengthen language grammar
preparation.detail: Revise parts of speech, tenses and comprehension from the Class 4–5 (or 7–8 for Class IX) books.

preparation.step: Build a General Knowledge notebook
preparation.detail: National symbols, defence, sports, awards and current personalities — revise weekly.

preparation.step: Solve past answer-keyed papers under 150/180 minutes
preparation.detail: Use the official final answer keys below to check your work; there is no negative marking, so attempt every question.

preparation.step: Prepare for the medical
preparation.detail: Admission also needs medical fitness — check the standards in the bulletin early.

faq.question: Have the AISSEE-2027 dates been announced?
faq.answer: Not as of 25 October 2026: the NTA website had no AISSEE-2027 notice. This page will show the dates once NTA publishes them.

faq.question: Can girls apply to Sainik Schools?
faq.answer: Yes, girls are eligible to apply. For approved New Sainik Schools, check the school’s own admission policy.

faq.question: Is there negative marking?
faq.answer: The AISSEE-2026 bulletin does not provide for negative marking, so it is worth attempting every question. Check the new bulletin each year.

exams.name: Rashtriya Indian Military College (RIMC) Entrance Examination – Class VIII
exams.conductingAuthority: RIMC, Dehradun (Ministry of Defence); online applications through NTA from the December 2026 cycle
exams.summary: Roughly 25 boys and 10 girls are admitted each term. Vacancies are allotted state-wise (generally one per state; Delhi has one). Selection is by written exam, viva-voce and medical examination.

content.forSchools: Rashtriya Indian Military College, Garhi Cantt, Dehradun — a residential military college preparing boys and girls for the Defence Forces
content.entryClassText: Class VIII (admissions every six months — January and July terms)
eligibility: For the July 2027 term: not less than 12½ and not more than 14 years old as on 01 July 2027 (revised criterion from the December 2026 cycle).
Studying in Class VII (or passed Class VII) in a recognised school at the time of joining.
Medically fit as per the prescribed standards.
Domicile of the state whose vacancy is applied for.

pattern.title: Stages

sections.name: Written examination — Mathematics and English (descriptive), General Knowledge (MCQs)

notes: Pen-and-paper test. Marks, duration and syllabus are in the NTA Information Bulletin for the cycle.

topics: As published in the RIMC/NTA notification for the cycle

selection: Written examination, then viva-voce, then medical examination, state-wise against the allotted vacancies.
content.fee: Exam fee (RIMCEE-2026): ₹1,000 for General, wards of Defence personnel and ex-servicemen, and OBC (NCL); ₹750 for SC/ST; paid online. College fee for boarder cadets (w.e.f. January 2024 term): ₹1,48,650 (General) / ₹1,31,850 (SC/ST) as listed, plus a refundable security of ₹50,000. Scholarships are listed on the RIMC website.

preparation.step: Check your state’s vacancy and the age window
preparation.detail: Usually one seat per state — competition is within your state.

preparation.step: Register on the NTA portal on time
preparation.detail: Keep Aadhaar, photo, domicile, birth and school-studying certificates scanned and ready.

preparation.step: Prepare for a written test and an interview
preparation.detail: Strong school-level Mathematics, English and General Knowledge, plus confident communication for the viva-voce.

preparation.step: Practise with the official past-papers booklet
preparation.detail: RIMC sells a booklet of the previous 7 years’ question papers (see below).

preparation.step: Meet the medical standards
preparation.detail: Read the RIMC medical standards early — unfit candidates are not admitted.

documents: Aadhaar card
Passport-size photograph
Domicile certificate
Birth certificate
Category certificate (if applicable)
School studying certificate
Scanned signature and left-thumb impression
Serving certificate (eligible Central Government employees)

faq.question: Can girls apply to RIMC?
faq.answer: Yes. RIMC admits both boys and girls; about 25 boys and 10 girls join each term.

faq.question: Where do I get the application form?
faq.answer: Only online through the NTA portal. RIMC and state governments do not issue forms.

papers.title: Question papers booklet — sold by RIMC for ₹300
papers.note: Pay via the QR code in RIMC’s notice; send the receipt and address to 9756201212 (WhatsApp) or rimcentexam@gmail.com

content.papersNote: RIMC does not publish free past papers online; it sells the official booklet. We do not reproduce its contents.
applicationSteps: Apply online only, through the NTA RIMCEE portal. No hard copy is needed, and forms are not available from RIMC or state governments.

Upload the documents within the stated timelines: Aadhaar, photograph, domicile certificate, birth certificate, category certificate (if applicable), school studying certificate, and scans of the signature and left-thumb impression.
Pay the exam fee online by credit or debit card, net banking or UPI.
Read the NTA Information Bulletin for the scheme, syllabus and other details before applying, and check the NTA website for updates.
examDay: The written test is pen and paper, at an NTA examination centre in one of 39 cities; your centre is on the admit card.

dates.label: Late submission with ₹500 late fee (5:00 p.m.)

exams.name: Netarhat Awasiya Vidyalaya Entrance Examination – Class 6
exams.conductingAuthority: Netarhat Awasiya Vidyalaya (Netarhat Vidyalaya Samiti, Govt. of Jharkhand)
exams.summary: A two-level written exam on one day at each divisional headquarters of Jharkhand, followed by a physical and psychological test, for 100 seats for boys. The application is free.

content.forSchools: Netarhat Awasiya Vidyalaya, Latehar, Jharkhand — a free residential school for boys, established 1954
eligibility: Boys aged 10–12 years as on 01 August 2026 — born 01.08.2014 to 31.07.2016 (both inclusive).
Native / local resident of Jharkhand (resident certificate required).
Passed Class 5 (or higher) from a recognised school in Jharkhand.
Category certificate if applying under a reserved category; all certificates must be attached.

pattern.title: Paper 1 — Preliminary (qualifying), 10:00 a.m. – 12:30 p.m.
notes: Objective MCQs, 1 mark each, on OMR; no negative marking.
Qualifying only: 5 × seats (500) are short-listed on merit as per reservation rules.

pattern.title: Paper 2 — Main (subjective), 1:30 p.m. – 4:00 p.m.
notes: Only the 500 short-listed candidates’ answer books are evaluated.
Questions are generally at Class 5 level; medium is Hindi and English.

topics: Questions are generally at the level of Class 5, answerable by meritorious Class 5 students

selection: Paper 1 short-lists 500 candidates (5 × seats); Paper 2 marks decide the next stage.
150 candidates (1.5 × seats) are called for a physical and psychological test, including age verification by a medical board.
Final 100 admitted on merit and reservation, after verification of all certificates.
content.fee: Application is free. The 2026-27 advertisement describes the school's education as free and residential, while the school's fee page says the State Government meets its costs and guardians pay a subsidised fee by income group (A–E). Ask the school which applies to new admissions.

preparation.step: Check domicile and age documents early
preparation.detail: A Jharkhand resident certificate, birth certificate and Class 5 pass certificate are mandatory — the form is rejected without them.

preparation.step: Prepare both objective and written answers
preparation.detail: Paper 1 is MCQs, but selection depends on the subjective Paper 2 — practise writing short answers in Hindi and English.

preparation.step: Master Class 5 textbooks
preparation.detail: Hindi, Mathematics, Science and Social Studies from the Class 5 books form the base of both papers.

preparation.step: Practise Mental Ability
preparation.detail: 20 marks in Paper 1 — series, analogies, odd-one-out and figure questions.

preparation.step: Solve the official sample papers
preparation.detail: Use the school’s sample papers below with a 2.5-hour timer for each paper.

preparation.step: Get ready for the interview stage
preparation.detail: Short-listed boys face a physical and psychological assessment of readiness for residential life.

documents: Jharkhand native / local resident certificate issued by the competent authority
Birth certificate issued by the competent authority
Class 5 (or higher) pass certificate signed by the head of the school
Caste / category certificate, if applying under a reserved category
Originals of all certificates at the time of admission

faq.question: Can girls apply to Netarhat Awasiya Vidyalaya?
faq.answer: No. Advertisement no. 262 invites applications from boys for 100 seats in Class 6.

faq.question: Is the application free?
faq.answer: Yes. The advertisement invites free (निःशुल्क) applications.

content.papersNote: These are the sample papers published by the school. No official answer keys or more recent papers are published on its website.

exams.name: Rashtriya Military Schools Common Entrance Test (CET) – Class VI & IX
exams.summary: An automated OMR-based common entrance test followed by interview. All admissions are as boarders — no day scholars. Applications are online (portal linked from the RMS website).

content.forSchools: Rashtriya Military Schools at Chail, Ajmer, Belgaum, Bengaluru and Dholpur — boarding schools affiliated to CBSE
eligibility: Class VI: not less than 10 and not more than 12 years as on 31 March of the year of admission.
Class IX: not less than 13 and not more than 15 years as on 31 March of the year of admission.
Admission against available vacancies; check the latest CET notification for whether girls are eligible (the RMS site’s admission page and its application link differ on this).

pattern.title: CET
notes: Subjects as listed in the CET notification.

topics: As published in the latest CET notification

selection: Merit in the CET, interview, medical fitness and reservation of vacancies as notified.
content.fee: Annual fee (revised, effective 2020-21): ₹12,000 (entitled OR category), ₹18,000 (JCO), ₹32,000 (non-entitled officers), ₹51,000 (non-entitled civilians); SC/ST pay 25% of their category fee; no tuition fee for wards of personnel killed in action.

preparation.step: Watch for the CET notification
preparation.detail: It is published in Employment News and on the RMS website; registration is online.

preparation.step: Prepare Mathematics, English, reasoning and GK
preparation.detail: Use school textbooks of the class you are completing; practise OMR-style timed tests.

preparation.step: Prepare for interview and medical
preparation.detail: Shortlisted candidates are interviewed; all admissions are residential.

faq.question: Are day scholars admitted to Rashtriya Military Schools?
faq.answer: No. All admissions are as boarders.

content.papersNote: The RMS website does not publish past question papers or answer keys, so none are listed.

exams.name: Eklavya Model Residential School Selection Test (EMRSST), Odisha – Class VI
exams.conductingAuthority: Odisha Model Tribal Education Society (OMTES), ST & SC Development, Minorities & Backward Classes Welfare Department, Government of Odisha
exams.summary: Entrance test for Class VI in Odisha's Eklavya Model Residential Schools — free CBSE, English-medium residential schools of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for children predominantly from tribal backgrounds. Separate merit lists for boys and girls.

content.forSchools: Eklavya Model Residential Schools in Odisha run by OMTES — 47 functional and 24 opening in 2026-27 (of 111 sanctioned), 30 boys and 30 girls per school in Class VI
content.entryClassText: Class VI (CBSE, English medium, NCERT syllabus)
eligibility: Children of families listed under the Socio Economic and Caste Census (SECC); an income certificate, PHH (rice) / Antyodaya / Annapurna card, or a self-declaration of family income below ₹2.5 lakh a year is needed.

A bonafide certificate from the current school — or, for children out of school or studying at home, a self-declaration attested by the Sarpanch, Block Education Officer or headmaster — or an NIOS registration/pass certificate.
Age limits and the seat reservation table follow the NESTS Admission Guidelines of 08.12.2025, which Odisha's guideline applies but does not reproduce — check them in the official notice.

pattern.title: One paper — 100 objective questions, 100 marks, 2 hours
notes: Questions test competencies at the Class V level prescribed by NCERT / SCERT / CBSE.
One mark per question; answers are ticked on the question booklet itself.
Divyang candidates get 30 minutes extra.

topics: Class V competencies as prescribed by NCERT / SCERT / CBSE

selection: Separate merit lists for boys and girls, published on omtes.odisha.gov.in.
Seats are filled through up to three merit lists; absentees lose their seat after notice.
In 2026-27 (EMRSST-II), results were due by 18 July, first-list admissions ran 27–31 July and second-list admissions 4–10 August 2026.
content.fee: No fee for the entrance examination. Education with residential facilities in EMRSs is provided free of cost by the Government of India.

preparation.step: Collect the income and school documents early
preparation.detail: The SECC/income proof and the school certificate are needed with the application.

preparation.step: Spend half your practice on Mental Ability
preparation.detail: It carries 50 of the 100 marks — figure series, analogies, odd-one-out and patterns.

preparation.step: Revise Class V Arithmetic and English
preparation.detail: The test is pitched at Class V competencies; practise reading short English passages.

documents: Income certificate (preferably e-District), PHH / Antyodaya / Annapurna card, or self-declaration of income below ₹2.5 lakh a year
Bonafide certificate from the current school, or attested self-declaration, or NIOS registration/pass certificate

faq.question: Have the 2027-28 dates been announced?
faq.answer: Not as of 26 October 2026. The 2026-27 dates are shown as an earlier cycle for reference.

faq.question: Is there an application fee?
faq.answer: No. The 2026-27 guideline says no fee is to be paid for the examination.

faq.question: Do EMRSs in other states use the same test?
faq.answer: No. Each state runs its own EMRS selection test with its own dates; this page covers Odisha only.

exams.name: Kendriya Vidyalaya admission (Class I lottery; Classes II–XI by vacancy, test or marks)
exams.summary: Admission to Kendriya Vidyalayas follows the KVS Admission Guidelines: Class I seats are filled by draw of lots (no test), Classes II–VIII by vacant seats in order of priority category, Class IX through an admission test, and Class XI on Class X board marks. Admission is open to all, not only children of Central Government employees.

content.forSchools: Kendriya Vidyalayas run by Kendriya Vidyalaya Sangathan — Central Government day schools affiliated to CBSE; Balvatika (pre-primary) in selected KVs
content.entryClassText: Balvatika 1–3 (selected KVs), Class I; Classes II–X and XII against vacant seats; Class XI
eligibility: Age on 31 March of the admission year: Class I 6 to under 8 years; II 7–9; III 8–10; IV 9–11; V 10–12; VI 10–12; VII 11–13; VIII 12–14; IX 13–15; X 14–16 (lower limit inclusive, upper limit exclusive).
Balvatika 1, 2 and 3: 3 to 4, 4 to 5 and 5 to 6 years as on 31 March (2026-27 notice).
Class XI: no age limit if seeking admission in the year of passing Class X.
The maximum age may be relaxed by two years for Children with Special Needs (CwSN).
Admissions are open to all; priority categories only decide the order in which applicants are admitted.

pattern.title: Class I — no test: seats filled by draw of lots
notes: First lot: 10 of the 40 seats per section (25%, under the RTE Act) by draw of lots among SC/ST/EWS/BPL/OBC-NCL/CwSN applicants resident in the neighbourhood.
Second lot: Children with Special Needs, by priority category.
Third lot: the remaining seats by priority category.

pattern.title: Classes II–VIII — no test: vacant seats by priority category
notes: The guidelines state that no admission test is conducted for Classes II to VIII; vacant seats are filled within the class strength in order of the parents' priority category.

pattern.title: Class IX — admission test: one paper, 3 hours, 100 marks
notes: Minimum 33% in aggregate to qualify; 25% for SC/ST/CwSN candidates.
A merit list is prepared separately for each priority category; only vacant seats are filled.

pattern.title: Class XI — on Class X board marks
notes: KV students are admitted first, by merit, up to 50 per class; streams (Science, Commerce, Humanities) are allotted on Class X CBSE marks.
Non-KV students are admitted to remaining seats on the same criteria, in order of priority category.
Ties: higher Mathematics marks, then Mathematics + Science together, then the older candidate.

topics: Hindi, English, Mathematics, Social Science and Science — 20 marks each

selection: Reservations in all fresh admissions: 15% SC, 7.5% ST, 27% OBC (Non-Creamy Layer); 3% of seats horizontally for Children with Special Needs.

Priority categories in Civil/Defence sector KVs: (1) children of Central Government employees and ex-servicemen; (2) employees of Central autonomous bodies, PSUs and institutes of higher learning; (3) State Government employees; (4) employees of State autonomous bodies, PSUs and institutes; (5) all others. Within a category, more transfers of the parent in the last 7 years gets preference.
Project-sector and IHL KVs give first priority to employees of the sponsoring project or institute.
Lists of registered, eligible, selected and waitlisted children are displayed on the school notice board and the Vidyalaya website.
Admission is refused if wrong or misleading information is found in the application.
content.fee: No fee is charged from children admitted under the 25% RTE quota; they keep the exemption up to Class VIII. Other fees follow the KVS fee structure published by KVS.

preparation.step: Find your priority category first
preparation.detail: It decides the order of admission for Classes I–VIII and XI; check it against the guidelines with your employer's details.

preparation.step: Collect documents before registration opens
preparation.detail: Birth certificate, category certificates and the parent's address proof are needed when you register.

preparation.step: For Class IX, revise the Class VIII syllabus in all five subjects
preparation.detail: The test has equal marks for Hindi, English, Mathematics, Social Science and Science.

documents: Class I: birth certificate issued by the authority competent to register births
Other classes: date of birth as recorded in the transfer certificate (up to Class VIII admission is possible without a TC if the birth certificate is from a Government body)
SC/ST/EWS/OBC-NCL/BPL certificate where applicable (a parent's certificate is accepted initially; the child's within 3 months)
CwSN certificate from the competent authority, where applicable
Address proof of the parent, at registration

faq.question: Is there an entrance test for Class I in a Kendriya Vidyalaya?
faq.answer: No. Class I seats are filled by draw of lots: first the RTE quota, then Children with Special Needs, then the remaining seats by priority category.

faq.question: Are KVs only for children of Central Government employees?
faq.answer: No. The guidelines say admissions are open to all; priority categories only set the order of admission.

faq.question: Which classes have an admission test?
faq.answer: Class IX: one 3-hour, 100-mark paper in five subjects. Classes II–VIII have no test, and Class XI uses Class X board marks.

faq.question: When will 2027-28 admissions open?
faq.answer: Not announced as of 26 October 2026. In 2026-27, online Class I registration ran from 20 March to 2 April 2026.

content.papersNote: KVS does not publish past Class IX admission test papers on its website, so none are listed.
applicationSteps: Class I and Balvatika: register online on the KVS admission portal during the registration window (2026-27: 20 March to 2 April 2026).
Classes II and above (except XI) and offline Balvatika: register offline at the Principal's office of the KV, only if that class has vacancies (2026-27: 2–8 April 2026).
Class XI: KV students register within 10 days of the Class X board result; non-KV students register for any seats left after KV students are admitted.
Contact the Principal or admission in-charge only when called, in the given time slot.
